title: Oak’s Aila saves primary teachers 49 minutes a week on lesson planning, EEF trial finds
source_used: EdTech Innovation Hub (reporting the EEF trial)
key_facts: An independent randomised controlled trial commissioned by the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF) and run by the National Foundation for Educational Research (NFER).
It tested Oak National Academy's Aila lesson assistant with Year 3 to Year 6 teachers in England for ten weeks in autumn 2025.
Aila users spent around 2.5 hours a week on preparation against 3.3 hours, about 49 minutes less.
Independent assessment found materials were no worse in quality.
81% used Aila at least once but it was used for only around 7% of lessons in an average week, and use declined.
Fewer than one in five teachers said it meaningfully changed their teaching or planning.
Oak's CEO said Oak's own earlier surveys suggested bigger savings than the trial found.
The EEF cautions that saving time does not automatically mean better teaching.
quote_evidence: Oak National Academy’s AI lesson assistant Aila saved primary teachers an average of around 49 minutes a week on lesson and resource preparation without reducing the quality of the materials they produced, according to a new independent randomized controlled trial.
The EEF cautions that saving planning time does not automatically mean better teaching.
why_it_matters_hint: An independent trial finds a real but modest time saving, with limited use.
